vault.title: Vault
vault.lockedIntro: Your bookmarks, history and open tabs are encrypted. Enter your password to decrypt them in this browser. Nothing is saved on this device: reloading the page, signing out or leaving it idle locks the vault again.
vault.unsupported: Some of your data uses an encryption format newer than this page can read. Update HelixSync to view it.
vault.readOnly: Read-only. To change anything, use the HelixSync extension.
vault.unreadableNote: {{n}} items couldn't be decrypted and are not shown.
vault.incompleteNote: {{n}} items are not shown because the server only holds a partial update for them.

login.deviceExpired: The sign-in request expired. Start a new one.
login.understandRequired: Please confirm that you understand how your password can be recovered.
login.deviceIntro: Open the HelixSync extension on a browser that's already connected to this account, and approve the request there. Approve it only if the extension shows this exact phrase:
login.insecureHttp: This page is not using HTTPS. HelixSync's session cookies are marked Secure, so browsers won't keep you signed in over plain HTTP, and your sign-in would travel unencrypted. Serve HelixSync over HTTPS (see docs/deployment.md).
login.registrationClosed: This server has registration disabled, so new accounts can't be created here. Sign in with an existing account, or ask whoever runs this server.
login.registerWarning: Your data is end-to-end encrypted with a key that's locked by your password, on your own devices. The server never sees your password, so nobody, including whoever runs this server, can reset it for you. After you register you'll get a recovery code: it's the only way to set a new password without losing your data.
login.understood: I understand that if I lose both my password and my recovery code, my data can't be recovered.
login.haveAccount: Already have an account? Sign in

recover.noPasskeyForEmail: No passkey is saved in this browser for that email. Choose your rescue file instead.
recover.enterEmailOrFile: Enter your email first, or choose your rescue file.

notice.keepOffline: Keep it offline, printed or in a password manager. Anyone with this code and your email can reset your password and read your synced data.
notice.typeLabel: Type your recovery code to confirm you saved it
notice.saveFailed: Couldn't record that on the server. Try again.

notice.passkeyExisting: Your passkey still holds your old code. Seal this new one with it.

kit.title: HelixSync recovery kit
kit.step1: Open the HelixSync sign-in page at the server address above.
kit.step3: Enter your account email and this recovery code, then pick a new password.
kit.warning: Each code works once: you get a new one after using it. Keep this kit offline and private; anyone with it and your email can reset your password and read your synced data.

security.title: Security
security.encryptionRequired: End-to-end encryption is required for this account. The server cannot read your synchronized browser data.
security.encryptionNotRequired: This server is not enforcing end-to-end encryption, so it would accept unencrypted data (REQUIRE_ENCRYPTION is off). Your devices still encrypt what they sync, but nothing on the server stops a client that doesn't. This setup is only appropriate for local development — see docs/encryption.md.
security.changePasswordInfo: Your data stays readable across a password change: the encryption key itself doesn't change, it's just re-secured under your new password (docs/encryption.md §2). Every device just needs to sign in again to pick it up — nothing needs to be reconnected or re-synced. Changing your password also signs out every other browser session on this account.
security.recoveryInfo: Your recovery code lets you set a new password from the sign-in page if you forget yours, without losing your data. Generate a new one if you lost it or think someone else has seen it; the old code stops working right away.
security.wrongPasswordRecovery: That password is incorrect. Your recovery code was not changed.
security.passkeyInfo: A passkey (fingerprint, OS PIN, phone or security key) can unlock your recovery code if you lose the printed copy. The sealed code stays in this browser and in a rescue file that is useless without your passkey. The passkey is tied to this site's address, and your recovery code stays the baseline.
security.dangerInfo: Deleting your account permanently removes everything stored on this server: your devices, all synced bookmarks, history and tabs, and every session. It can't be undone, and because your data is encrypted with a key only your password unlocks, it can't be recovered afterwards either. Browsers that are still connected simply stop syncing.
security.wrongPasswordDelete: That password is incorrect. Nothing was deleted.

restore.title: Restore points
restore.unsupported: This server doesn't support restore points yet.
restore.intro: Saved, encrypted copies of your bookmarks. To restore one, open the HelixSync extension in your browser: restoring needs your account key, which this page never has.
restore.automaticHelp: A daily copy, plus one before a restore, a first import, a full resync, or a large deletion. Pin a point to keep it; unpinned ones are removed first when space runs out or after the retention period.
restore.deleteConfirm: Delete the restore point from {{date}}? This can't be undone.

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Encrypted copies of the whole server database, made by the server itself. Everyone with an account on this server sees this page. Restoring is done by the server's operator on the host; it can't be done from here.
backups.unsupported: This server doesn't support this page yet.
backups.off: Backups are turned off on this server (BACKUP_ENABLED=false).
backups.offMissingKey: Backups are turned off on this server. The operator turns them on by setting BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
backups.offInvalidKey: Backups are turned off on this server: its BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY is too short or still a placeholder. The operator turns them on by setting a valid key.
backups.failedHelp: A failed run is tried again after an hour; the server log says why.
backups.commandsIntro: For the server's operator, run on the host from the folder with the Compose file. Stop the server before restoring.

cmd.listBackups: List backup files (name, time, size, kind)
cmd.restoreNewest: Restore the newest scheduled or manual backup

rulesets.title: Rulesets
rulesets.intro: A ruleset is a named list of rules: folders not to sync, folders to sync exclusively, domains and address patterns to keep out of history, and local addresses. Assign devices to rulesets; each device applies the combined rules of all its rulesets. Rulesets are encrypted in your browser with your account key, so the server only stores them as ciphertext.
rulesets.forwardOnly: Changes apply from now on: history and bookmarks already synced are not removed. Extensions older than the first version with rulesets ignore them.
rulesets.defaultNote: Every new device joins this ruleset. It has no rules until you add some, and it can't be deleted or renamed.
rulesets.unreadable: This ruleset couldn't be decrypted, so it can't be shown or edited. It may have been changed by something other than HelixSync.
rulesets.patternPlaceholder: Regular expression, tested against the full address
rulesets.patternNote: Case-insensitive. Up to 20 patterns of 200 characters per ruleset.
rulesets.localNote: localhost, *.localhost, *.local, *.test, *.internal, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1 and the private IPv4 ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16).
rulesets.folderNote: Don't sync a folder, or sync only the folders you choose. A folder that is not synced stays on its devices; nothing is deleted. The rule follows the folder when it is renamed or moved.
rulesets.deleteConfirm: Delete this ruleset? Its devices stop applying its rules.
rulesets.conflict: This ruleset was changed elsewhere. Reload to see the latest version; your edits here are lost.
rulesets.refineSearch: More devices match: refine the search.
rulesets.tooOldNote: This device's extension is too old to apply rulesets (or its version is unknown). Update the extension on it.
rulesets.pickDevice: Pick a device to see its rulesets and test an address.
rulesets.notInAny: This device is in no ruleset: nothing is filtered.
rulesets.testHeading: Test an address on this device
rulesets.testFolderNote: Only address rules are tested here; folder rules apply to bookmarks.
